note: The angles, times, plane, rotation, elbow and suggested muscles below are TEST VALUES for checking the animation. They are typical textbook-style numbers, not researched and not checked by a clinician. No citation belongs to them. The animation never goes past the stated allowed range. Urdu and Roman Urdu are machine-written and need a native speaker's review.
conventions: elevation: angle of the upper arm from the model's rest pose, positive = up, negative = backward. plane: direction of elevation, 0 = side, 90 = forward, 30 = scapular plane. rotation: about the long axis of the upper arm, positive = external. elbow: flexion, 0 = straight. t: fraction of the loop. Hold = two frames with equal values.

movements.kinematicsNote: PLACEHOLDER values, flagged for physiotherapist review. Shoulder extension about 30 to 50 degrees with a little adduction (plane 80), internal rotation 80 to 90 degrees, elbow flexion up to about 85 degrees. The order matters: the arm goes back first, then rotates inward, then the elbow bends so the hand passes behind the pelvis, then it slides up the lower back to about lumbar level, holds about 1 second, and returns by the same way, slower. Checked against the trunk surface for interpenetration (see docs/movement-ux-findings.md).
movements.movementNote: Adapted from clinician-administered positions (lift-off / Apley scratch); self-administered version not validated.
movements.allowedNote: The ranges of Appendix A (appendixAllowed) are for the final position only. This movement now passes through the path described in kinematicsNote, so its working ranges are wider (elevation to -50, rotation to -90, elbow from 0). A physiotherapist must confirm both.

cameraNote: Camera presets are for the RIGHT side (position, target, fov, zoom; metres). The left side mirrors x. They are placeholder framings, to be reviewed on a phone. Timing: out, hold about 1 second at the end pose, slower return.
